name: gather-pleat
title: Gather Pleat
description: Middle truncation as fabric: a long path, URL or hash gathers its hidden middle into a narrow pleated band whose fold count is proportional to how many characters it hides. Click, drag or Enter pulls the pleat open on a spring, revealing the full run without ever moving the head or tail.
useWhen: a table cell, header, or log line needs to truncate the MIDDLE of a path, URL or hash while keeping both ends readable, and the still frame should communicate roughly how much is hidden — the pleat's fold density scales with the hidden character count, and it's directly pullable (click, drag, or Enter) to reveal the exact middle in place. Distinct from vanish-taper (fades and crowds the trailing END of a line, and never states a quantity or offers a middle reveal) and selvage-fold (clamps whole PARAGRAPH lines by word count, not a single inline string's middle).
instruction: A middle-truncation primitive for file paths, URLs and hashes: the informative parts of a long identifier are usually its two ends, but a hard '...' clip only ever admits 'something was cut,' never how much or where the loss concentrates. Required prop `text` is the full string, always rendered as real, complete DOM text in document order (head span, hidden-middle span, tail span) — clipping is a CSS width/overflow effect on the middle span only, never a removed or aria-hidden node, so assistive tech, find-in-page and copy/paste always see the whole string regardless of visual state. MEASUREMENT: `headChars` (default 10) and `tailChars` (default 8) characters are always shown in full at each end (counted over Array.from graphemes, so surrogate pairs never split); everything between them is the hidden run. If the hidden run is shorter than `minHidden` (default 4) characters, the component renders the plain string with no pleat and no control at all — truncation machinery never appears on text that doesn't need it. THE PLEAT: hidden-character count drives fold count (one fold per ~3 hidden characters, clamped 2-14), and fold count drives the collapsed strip width (~6.5px per fold) — a lightly-clipped cell shows a slim two-fold band, a badly-clipped one shows a dense shirred strip, so the resting frame communicates magnitude the way a stitched hem communicates how much fabric was gathered. The pleat glyph itself is N diagonal SVG line segments (stroke currentColor, colored via the --border token, intensifying to --muted on hover) zigzagging across the strip, over an opaque --background backdrop rect that fully occludes the clipped text underneath at rest. MECHANISM: the pleat is a single real <button> absolutely positioned over the width-animated middle strip — its paint IS the fold glyph, not a separate decorative layer. Click or Enter toggles between the collapsed fold width and the middle text's natural (measured via a hidden, non-participating measurer clone) un-clipped width, on a 420ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) spring; opening fades the backdrop and fold strokes out in a left-to-right stagger (each fold's transition-delay increases with its index) while a dashed baseline seam fades in once the strip finishes opening — a residual, always-visible, non-transparent affordance so the open state never disappears to nothing. Closing reverses both: the strip springs back to its fold width while the folds fade back in right-to-left and the seam retreats. DRAG: pointerdown on the button then moving the pointer horizontally maps that delta 1:1 onto the strip's width (clamped between the collapsed and natural widths, transition suppressed for direct 1:1 tracking) — a partial drag lets a sighted, pointing user peek however many hidden characters they want without committing to a full open; releasing past the ResizeObserver-measured midpoint snaps to fully open, short of it snaps back closed, on the same spring. A small movement threshold (4px) distinguishes a drag from a plain click so both gestures coexist on one control without double-toggling. Head and tail characters never move during any of this — only the strip between them changes width. ACCESSIBILITY: the button carries `aria-expanded` and an accessible name stating the exact hidden count ('31 characters hidden, expand' / 'collapse') — never a bare icon description. Escape collapses an open pleat while it's focused. REDUCED MOTION: every transition (width spring, fold stagger, backdrop and seam fades) is disabled via prefers-reduced-motion — toggling and dragging still work, they just snap instantly to their end state rather than animating. Colors are tokens only: --background for the occlusion backdrop, --border/--muted for the fold strokes (default/hover), --foreground for all real text, --accent only as the focus ring. Zero runtime dependencies, DOM + SVG + CSS only, no canvas.
